event.summary: Replacement SIGCONT has a spec-accepted short PID-reuse window
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: If the old server exits and its pid is reused immediately after SIGTERM, the following SIGCONT could resume an unrelated stopped process. The original consequence remains; no wrong-target execution was observed. Suggested bucket: other for the source-supported SIGCONT possibility. Could-be-highest: uncertain; security or work-loss consequences would require a harmful unrelated stopped process and immediate PID reuse, neither established in a shipped scenario. Confidence: confirmed source sequence with a hypothetical reuse premise, explicitly accepted by specification, not reproduced. Lead resolution: hosts/process.rs:416–452 documents the SIGTERM/SIGCONT/SIGKILL sequence and explicitly states that SIGCONT follows SIGTERM without its own check. git diff of this file between the reviewed commit and its parent is empty; the sequence is not introduced by the assigned deletion. terminate_process_within at 490–498 sends SIGTERM and SIGCONT back-to-back with no intervening await or unbounded work; SIGKILL at 502–507 revalidates after its await. proposed_drop: exact SPEC_impl.md:5105–5118 acceptance, under Runtime state, says: "Code that signals or adopts a process by its number may lose the race in which that process exits and the kernel hands the number to an unrelated process within a short, bounded window: between reading a number and checking it, between reaping a child and signalling its group, while a watchdog fires just as its child finishes, or during a polling loop of at most a few seconds." It further says: "What is not accepted is carrying a bare number across unbounded waits or asynchronous work, or storing it for later." (line wraps normalized only). The back-to-back continuation signal fits the short accepted window; the source's own termination docstring cites this exact specification acceptance. possible_cover: none beyond that specification rule.
